name: MW-SENSE
intent: Create an MW-SENSE simulation using ESP32 with DHT22 temperature and humidity sensor along with air quality and soil moisture sensors. Simulate WiFi and MQTT transmission to a centralized live monitoring dashboard, with automatic updates, error detection and future sensor nodes.
programming: Run the compiled ESP32 firmware in the 3D simulator; USB serial flashing for a physical ESP32 DevKit V1.
acceptance: ESP32 connected to DHT22, air-quality and soil moisture sensors with correct GPIO and power wiring.
Firmware collects and validates sensor readings with automatic updates and error detection.
WiFi and MQTT transmit sensor data to a centralized dashboard displaying live values and sensor status.
Additional sensor nodes can be added in future.

assumed.why: USB-powered development board; sensors supplied by its 3.3V output.

notes: Selected 3D breadboard and ESP32 DevKit V1 30-pin. SGP40 VOC breakout for relative air-quality trends, not certified AQI or CO2; capacitive soil moisture v1.2 at 3.3V with real-probe calibration required. DHT22 DATA GPIO13 with 10k pullup; SGP40 SDA21/SCL22; soil AOUT GPIO34 ADC1. All sensor power inputs at3.3V, common ground; SGP40 3V3 output left unconnected.
